audit.summary: The library correctly keeps ONE BOX as base, one immutable layout authority per run, proposal-only model output, browser REJECT until EB-001–EB-021, GSAP/appointment/provider stops, and no implementation authorization. It must be revised before acceptance because operating-environment draft work is scheduled as if authorized, retained Electron/E0 shell is not consistently blocked by EB-001, T4 freezes the rejected E4.0–E4.7 decomposition, E7 React/ExperienceModule targets collide with Page IR static-site authority, and the starred/technology catalogs disagree on dispositions, phases, and Adopt vs Needs-license-review.

findings.constraint: docs/audits/grok-4.6/2026-08-29-embedded-browser-plan-audit.md — Required correction order 1 / EB-001; docs/plans/one-box-master/README.md Current stop conditions
findings.issue: The operating-environment index lets read-only E0–E3 proceed in parallel and names E0 as a desktop shell, while only E4 is marked blocked. The adoption matrix meanwhile places Electron at E0 shell and E4.0/E4.1 only after EB-001. Those statements cannot both be true. Grok required hostile-page isolation before any retained desktop shell, not merely before a later Browser workspace.
findings.scenario: A team treats 04-index parallel E0 as authorization, ships a retained Electron shell around the loopback app with no EB-001 partition/navigation oracle, then later attaches WebContentsView. A hostile page navigates to the app origin, loopback, or file URL and inherits trusted-renderer session/credentials.
findings.correction: Define E0 as identity/role/sync contracts only. State that any retained Electron/native shell, packaging, or remote-content host is blocked until a rewritten browser plan closes EB-001–EB-021, starting with EB-001. Keep disposable out-of-tree spikes report-only.

findings.constraint: docs/plans/one-box-master/00-authority/plan-register.md — Team, agents, skills, browser, and desktop shell; Conflict rule; docs/plans/one-box-master/README.md Current stop conditions
findings.issue: The register labels the operating-environment design an architecture draft that cannot weaken website or appointment contracts, and the README says drafts remain evidence. The 04 index and T3 still publish E0–E3 as the expansion/adoption sequence, including Agent Studio, skills, CRDT drafts, and a desktop shell. That upgrades a draft into program authority.
findings.scenario: An implementation plan cites 04-index E1–E3 as scheduled work, adds cloud identity, model registry, and Yjs surfaces, and treats the draft as accepted architecture. Website candidate/release contracts are then extended from an unauthorized design.
findings.correction: Mark E0–E8 in the master index as draft decomposition only. Require a separate accepted operating-environment spec and implementation plan before any retained E0–E3 work. Keep T3 items as research/pattern notes until that gate.

findings.section: T4, embedded browser and governed reconstruction
findings.constraint: docs/audits/grok-4.6/2026-08-29-embedded-browser-plan-audit.md — Verdict REJECT, EB-001 through EB-021, Required correction order 2
findings.issue: T4 correctly waits for a corrected plan, then restates the rejected E4.0–E4.7 slice list (containment spike, unified tabs, CDP observation, guarded interactions, reconstruction, agent browser skills) as the lane. The Grok audit required rewriting E4.0/E4.1 gates for hostile isolation, composition, navigation policy, hardening, and oracles before retained work. Copying the rejected decomposition makes the uncorrected plan a second sequence authority.
findings.scenario: After a narrow EB-001 note, implementers execute T4 E4.0/E4.1 as written, omit rewritten hostile-page, occlusion, keyboard, fuse, and recovery oracles, and treat T4 exit language as satisfaction of EB-002–EB-021.
findings.correction: Replace the T4 slice list with: no E4 sequence is authoritative until a corrected plan maps each of EB-001–EB-021 to an owner, oracle, and exit gate. Do not reuse E4.0–E4.7 numbering until that rewrite is accepted.

findings.section: T5, client room, stack intelligence, and premium modules — E7
findings.constraint: docs/specs/2026-08-22-page-ir-safe-pipeline-prd.md — Decision summary 3–4, REQ-IR-003, REQ-LAY-001/002, Architecture (static website candidate); docs/plans/one-box-master/01-foundation/index.md Locked foundation
findings.issue: T5 delivers a compiler registry with static and React targets plus signed ExperienceModules. 02-canvas E7 likewise adds stack selection and allowlisted modules for behavior Page IR cannot express. Phase 1 Page IR is a single deterministic static-website compiler; Page IR cannot carry executable HTML/CSS/JS, and outside frameworks cannot introduce a second site document/runtime model. React/Next and module-shipped JS are a second production authority unless explicitly subordinated and deferred.
findings.scenario: E7 selects a React/Next target or signed ExperienceModule as the generated site runtime. Models or designers then edit module/React source instead of typed Page IR. Qualification and promotion attach to a second document model, violating one-authority-per-run.
findings.correction: Strike React as a Track A compiler/document model. Keep Page IR static compilation as the only site source. Confine R3F/GSAP/WebGL to later signed ExperienceModules that cannot author or bypass Page IR, and only after Phase 1 exit plus a separate schema/security plan.

findings.issue: T5 and the shipping roadmap require P3 (review-origin threat model, scoped session, invitation, candidate-lock, revocation) before LiveKit/E6. The 04 index lists E6 after E5, states only E4 is blocked, and never restates the P3 gate. Followers of the operating-environment front door can invert client-review and media-room order.
findings.scenario: E6 LiveKit rooms are built against draft operating-environment acceptance criteria. Guests receive screen share and candidate view before P3 invitation-exchange, non-indexable review origin, and lock/revocation oracles exist. A review URL or room token becomes a second client-access path.
findings.correction: In 04-index, gate E6 on accepted P3 exit criteria. Repeat T5 language: LiveKit is media transport only after P3; it cannot create review, lock, or invitation authority.

findings.section: E1 / E5 / E8 tables versus relevance report Immediate phase anchors and Relevant inventory
findings.issue: The same snapshot assigns incompatible dispositions and phases. t3code is Adapt in the shortlist/matrix and Learn only in the relevance report/JSON. supermemory is Learn only in the shortlist and Adapt in relevance/JSON. strix is Learn in the shortlist/matrix and Adapt in relevance/JSON. hyperframes is E5 in the shortlist and E7 in relevance/JSON. Instatic is P5/E8 with no E7 publishing authority in the shortlist/roadmap and Existing Canvas lifecycle + E7 in relevance/JSON. livekit/agents is Adapt for E6 in relevance while the matrix adopts LiveKit only as post-P3 media transport.
findings.scenario: An implementer uses the relevance report's Adapt labels, imports t3code/strix/livekit-agents or Instatic publish/CMS paths, and treats the shortlist's tighter bounds as optional commentary.
findings.correction: Make the shortlist the only planning disposition table. Reconcile JSON/relevance to those labels, or mark relevance as superseded metadata. Demote livekit/agents to Learn only; keep LiveKit SFU as the P3-gated media layer.

findings.section: Quality, SEO, publishing, and operations — PostHog; License and security stop list
findings.constraint: docs/plans/one-box-master/06-technology/index.md Decision classes — Needs license review; docs/plans/one-box-master/06-technology/technology-adoption-roadmap.md T0 fail-closed on mixed licenses
findings.issue: Needs license review means no code-level use until resolved. PostHog is Adapt-through-SDK in the matrix/shortlist and Needs license review / mixed license in relevance, JSON, and the stop list. agent-native is in the E1 shortlist as Learn/adapt-contract while SPDX is unavailable. React Three Fiber is Adopt in relevance/JSON and only Conditional adopt after Page IR qualification in the matrix.
findings.scenario: A T3/E8 plan adds posthog-js or copies agent-native hooks because the shortlist/matrix say Adapt, before mixed-license/SPDX review, and later cannot remove enterprise or unaudited terms from the desktop build.
findings.correction: Reclassify PostHog and agent-native as Needs license review with no Adapt/Adopt until a license receipt exists. Keep R3F as Conditional adopt only inside a qualified ExperienceModule, including in the relevance/JSON columns.

findings.section: Coverage and method; Immediate phase anchors
findings.issue: Counts 133 / 107 / 18 are internally consistent (category census 48+14+5+13+6+10+4+7=107; 107+26=133; shortlist has 18 named repos). Narrowing is not. Relevance Immediate phase anchors treat semantica as an E1 Adapt source and t3code as an E1 control-surface source, but semantica is absent from the 18-item shortlist and t3code's disposition conflicts. fontsource/font-files is Adopt in relevance/JSON and missing from the shortlist and matrix. Exclusion rules beyond a vague source-and-license pass are not stated.
findings.scenario: Planning uses Immediate phase anchors, adds semantica or fontsource as Adopt/Adapt, and bypasses the claimed source-checked shortlist.
findings.correction: Publish exclusion criteria for the 107→18 cut. Remove Immediate phase anchors that are not on the shortlist. Move any true Adopt candidate into the matrix with phase, license receipt, and oracle, or demote fontsource to Evaluate/Learn only.

findings.constraint: docs/plans/one-box-master/README.md Current stop conditions — GSAP; docs/research/source-catalog/one-box-technology-adoption-matrix-2026-08-29.md GSAP 3.15; docs/plans/one-box-master/00-authority/plan-register.md Supporting — prompt-driven engine decisions
findings.issue: A4 includes bounded motion while GSAP visual motion authoring is a hard stop pending written consent, and Motion is only Evaluate as a later default runtime. Neither 02-canvas nor T3 binds A4 motion to that stop or names a non-GSAP oracle.
findings.scenario: A4 implements a visual motion builder on existing GSAP usage because prompt-engine decisions previously selected it. That continues competing no-code motion authoring before license review.
findings.correction: Split A4 motion into non-builder defaults already in tree versus any visual motion-authoring UI. Block the latter on GSAP consent or a Motion evaluate-and-replace plan with a removal path.

findings.section: Decision; Model and runtime shortlist — Qwen3.5-4B / Apple MLX; Adopt into the benchmark corpus — WebInfinity
findings.constraint: docs/plans/one-box-master/06-technology/technology-adoption-roadmap.md T1 exit; docs/research/source-catalog/README.md Rules for use; docs/plans/one-box-master/06-technology/index.md Decision classes
findings.issue: The HF note says do not adopt a model runtime yet, then Adopts MLX (and E1-if-accepted) and cites a community MLX 4-bit conversion without its own pin/license/hash. WebInfinity is listed under Adopt into the benchmark corpus while its limitation is unfinished provenance audit. Qwen/PaddleOCR/Florence phases are E4.3/E4.5, which are blocked, without restating that T1 measurements are research-only fixtures.
findings.scenario: T1 operators download the community 4-bit Qwen conversion or WebInfinity pages, later promote mlx-vlm into E1 because MLX is Adopt, and feed unreviewed generated pages or unpinned weights into reconstruction proposals.
findings.correction: Classify MLX as Evaluate for the research harness only. Require official or counsel-reviewed conversion hashes before any local weight is used. Keep WebInfinity out of the offline corpus until rights/provenance review. Label all HF model rows Research/T1 until E4 is unblocked.

findings.constraint: docs/plans/one-box-master/00-authority/plan-register.md Conflict rule — a model audit cannot authorize implementation
findings.issue: The Canvas index lists the Grok canvas master-plan reconciliation audit as a canonical source beside owner-approved specs. Audits are evidence, not product authority.
findings.scenario: A later plan treats audit recommended order or PROCEED_WITH_CONDITIONS as a substitute for Page IR or Canvas-upgrade requirements.
findings.correction: Move the audit to supporting/historical evidence. Keep only owner-approved specs as Canvas canonical sources.

accepted_decisions: Retain ONE BOX as the base project; Puck, GrapesJS, Webstudio, Onlook, Craft.js, and OpenPage are not replacement foundations.
One immutable layout authority per run: page-ir-v1 or guarded template-v1; never merge or switch inside a run.
Models emit typed proposals only; deterministic compile, gates, candidate identity, and human approval remain authoritative.
Embedded browser stays REJECT / NOT_AUTHORIZED until EB-001–EB-021 are closed, starting with hostile-page isolation.
GSAP visual motion authoring is stopped pending written consent or license review.
Yjs/CRDT limited to draft PRDs, notes, comments, cursors, and awareness; no CRDT merge of Page IR, approvals, or release state.
P5 Release Orchestrator owns publishing; Instatic is a subordinate protocol after P1/P3/P4 and explicit P5 authorization, with no E7 publishing authority.
Production provider selection is only at P6; appointment implementation remains unauthorized until separate acceptance.
ST-WebAgentBench stays outside the offline corpus and requires a separately authorized sandboxed integration.
AGPL/GPL sources (Webstudio, Firecrawl, Plane, OpenMontage, ComfyUI) and CloakBrowser anti-detection are rejected for code reuse.
Catalog entries and the technology roadmap authorize no dependency or implementation by themselves.
audit.base_project_assessment: The retain-ONE-BOX decision is supported by the supplied comparison and by Page IR constraints. Puck is correctly held as a behind-IR interaction experiment, GrapesJS as HTML/CSS-authority conflict, Webstudio as AGPL plus alternate document model, Onlook as file/code ownership conflict, Craft.js as extra editor state (maintenance claim is not evidenced here), and OpenPage as immature direct-output authority. No supplied artifact shows an external editor that preserves candidate identity, typed mutations, and one layout authority per run. Do not re-platform.
audit.star_coverage_assessment: Numeric coverage is consistent: JSON/REST/GraphQL claim 133, relevance census sums to 107 relevant plus 26 unrelated, and the shortlist names 18 repositories. Identity/disposition coverage is not. The 107→18 cut is not reproducible from stated rules, Immediate phase anchors disagree with the shortlist (semantica, t3code), and Adapt/Learn/Adopt/phase labels diverge for t3code, supermemory, strix, PostHog, hyperframes, Instatic, R3F, and fontsource. The relevance pass is metadata/README triage, which the report itself says is not a source or security audit. Treat only a reconciled shortlist as planning input.

residual_risks: Adopt/Adapt labels will be read as dependency authorization despite catalog disclaimers.
Metadata-only starred triage will be treated as a source or security audit.
Community model conversions and trust_remote_code revisions can drift after T1 pins if upgrade policy is not enforced.
ExperienceModules can reintroduce executable site authority even if React is struck as a compiler target.
Draft operating-environment product promises (cloud identity, Auto routing, client rooms) will pull work ahead of website Track A.
